caseno: Appeal From Original Decree (FA) No. 87 of 1987.
lawyer:
Md Ohiullah, Advocate---For the Appellant. 
Snigdha Huq, Deputy Attorney-General---For the Respondent.
parties:
Commerce Tanker Corporation and another ----- Appellants
Vs
Government of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh ----- Respondent
full_judgment: 4. The defendants appeared and submitted the written statement denying the allegations made in the plaint stating that the suit is not maintainable in its present form. The plaintiff has no power, the suit is barred by limitation and for the defect of parties stated that the alleged shortage of delivery is totally a myth and false and that there was no physical verification and defilement of the discharged cargo and that the entire wheat was delivered at Chittagong and Chalna and that the ship after arrival at Chalna was at the disposal of the Customs authority and the plaintiff's stevedore effected the delivery of the cargo and there is no shootage of delivery at Chittagong or Chalna. In support of their contention, they produced Exhibit-'A', 'Al' and 'B'. The certificate was issued by the authority. After framing the issues, the plaintiff's examined one witness and the defendants examined one witness. On 18-7-1973 Sunamuddin Sikder, an employee under the plaintiff proposed that the Government imported 25,132.132 tonnes of wheat and they have inspected 25,132.132 tonnes of wheat which have arrived in the ship 'ST Barbara' and at last reached Chittagong port and transshipped to lighter vessel 'SS Panagiotisk' for carrying to Chalna Port and on arrival, there was survey by Lloyd's Surveyor and it was ascertained 9,542 tonnes are there. After dis-charge of the vessel another survey was arranged by the Shipping Agents and they ascertained 9,511 tonnes. The lighter vessel, 'SS Panagiotisk' reached Chalna on 8-9-1968 and finally discharged those on 28-8-1968 and actual delivery was found to be 9,271 tonnes and there was shortage of delivery of 270 tonnes. They have filed claim notice dated 28-9-1968 Exhibit-1 and la. He has also put the survey report Exhibit-2 that the defendant did not pay the amount to the government for the loss. He denied the suggestion that there is no short delivery of the food grains. In cross-examination, he has stated that he has no personal knowledge. He also stated in cross-examination that he has no paper of first weighment. He also admitted that he was not connected with the disputed transaction and has no personal knowledge. On the other hand, DW 1, Md Ataur Rahman deposed that he is an employee of the defendant and has been working as shipping assistant for limited purpose. He stated that the entire food grains were discharged at Chittagong and Chalna. He proved the Exhibit-A, A(2) & B the certificate of Assistant Collector of Customs. There are no allegations as regards to the weighment. In cross-examination, he has also stated that he is serving under DW 2 for 10 years and joined in the shipping branch in 1965. Operation in Chittagong 12-8-1972 till with the discharge of the main ship to the lighter vessel.
